hints.title: Small Output Space
hints.text: Valid answers are strictly three-digit even integers, spanning only the values from 100 to 998 with step two.

hints.title: Target-First Validation
hints.text: Rather than permuting the input array, test each of the 450 even candidates against the available digit counts.

hints.title: Digit Availability Check
hints.text: Decompose each candidate into hundreds, tens, and units digits and verify if the input contains sufficient quantities.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def findEvenNumbers(self, digits: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        available = Counter(digits)
        ans = []

        for num in range(100, 1000, 2):
            d1, rem = divmod(num, 100)
            d2, d3 = divmod(rem, 10)

            need = Counter([d1, d2, d3])
            if all(available[d] >= count for d, count in need.items()):
                ans.append(num)

        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Inspect all 3-digit even numbers from 100 to 998 step 2 and verify digit frequency availability.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all permutations with backtracking requires sorting and deduplicating up to N^3 candidates.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterating through the 450 valid targets directly guarantees sorted and unique results.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should realize that checking 450 candidates against a frequency map is O(1).
